claim_being_audited: The Actor claims the model can be certified for launch, albeit weakly and with heavy qualification, because aggregate readiness passes, rehearsal showed no severity-one incidents, and a 3% reversible rollout plus monitoring can support launch despite an exposed below-target health-plan benefits support segment.

concern_ledger.concern: The affected health-plan benefits support segment remains below target and exposed in the initial rollout.
concern_ledger.evidence_needed_to_close: Configuration or cohort evidence proving exclusion of the affected use case from launch, or updated evaluations showing the segment meets target.
concern_ledger.why_it_blocks_compliance: The policy permits mitigation by rollout controls only if the affected use case is excluded or covered by reviewed risk acceptance. Exposure of the weak segment leaves the policy predicate unsatisfied.

concern_ledger.concern: There is no approved risk acceptance covering the exposed weak segment.
concern_ledger.evidence_needed_to_close: A signed reviewed risk-acceptance record that specifically addresses health-plan benefits support exposure and explains why launch exposure is acceptable.
concern_ledger.why_it_blocks_compliance: The existing draft is unsigned and omits the relevant exposure, so it cannot satisfy the policy exception that would permit launch despite the material weakness.

concern_ledger.concern: The record does not show completed pre-launch disclosure of the material limitation for the named launch use case.
concern_ledger.evidence_needed_to_close: A finalized model card or equivalent launch documentation showing the limitation was disclosed before certification/launch.
concern_ledger.why_it_blocks_compliance: The release policy requires disclosure unless the issue is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. The Actor describes a need for immediate documentation, which implies the required disclosure is not yet evidenced as complete.

concern_ledger.concern: The Actor treats aggregate readiness and reversible rollout controls as sufficient support for certification despite a direct contrary policy condition.
concern_ledger.evidence_needed_to_close: Admissible evidence satisfying the policy exception or removing the exposure, not merely additional monitoring rationale.
concern_ledger.why_it_blocks_compliance: Aggregate readiness and rollback evidence support operational caution, but do not satisfy the explicit compliance condition governing exposed material weaknesses.

decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence satisfies the policy threshold for certification.
If a material weakness remains, rollout controls help only when the affected use case is excluded or reviewed risk acceptance specifically justifies exposure.
A rollback switch, dashboard, or small launch percentage does not remove disclosure duties when the affected segment remains exposed.
General public guidance on monitoring and model cards can support governance posture, but cannot substitute for the missing internal policy predicate or required approval/disclosure artifact.
evidence_requests: Produce finalized pre-launch model-card disclosure that expressly covers the health-plan benefits support limitation for the named launch use case.
Produce approved risk acceptance, signed by the proper approver, that specifically addresses health-plan benefits support exposure in the initial rollout.
Produce rollout configuration evidence showing the affected use case is excluded from launch exposure.
Produce updated evaluation evidence showing the health-plan benefits support segment is no longer below target on benefits-eligibility explanation.
specific_concerns: The affected health-plan benefits support segment remains below target and is still exposed in the initial rollout cohort.

The governing policy text says rollout controls and monitoring mitigate a material model-card weakness only if the affected use case is excluded or reviewed risk acceptance explains why exposure is acceptable; neither predicate is satisfied here.
The risk-acceptance draft is unsigned and does not mention the exposed health-plan benefits support segment, so it is not admissible support for launch approval.

The release policy requires disclosure of material limitations for named launch use cases unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch; the packet does not show that disclosure is already completed before certification.
The Actor overrelies on general public guidance about monitoring and model-card documentation, which does not override the specific internal pre-launch policy condition.
unsupported_claims: That certification is supportable on the present record, even weakly, despite the exposed below-target segment and absence of approved risk acceptance or completed disclosure.
That a 3% rollout, rollback switch, and monitoring materially cure the disclosure-policy failure while the affected use case remains exposed.
That public governance guidance supplies sufficient support for certification under this case's specific policy predicates.
